open_release.rationale: The paper is motivated by data sharing and evaluates privacy attacks on the synthetic output, though without a formal DP guarantee.

quotes.text: Privacy concerns often arise as the key bottleneck for the sharing of data between consumers and data holders, particularly for sensitive data such as Electronic Health Records (EHR).
We propose a generative modeling framework, EHR-Safe, for generating highly realistic and privacy-preserving synthetic EHR data.

pipeline_testing.rationale: No test-data or development-data framing in the paper.

ml_augmentation.rationale: The paper evaluates train-on-synthetic, test-on-real mortality prediction.

quotes.text: we demonstrate that the fidelity of EHR-Safe is almost-identical with real data (<3% accuracy difference for the models trained on them) while yielding almost-ideal performance in practical privacy metrics.

statistical_replication.rationale: Per-feature statistical similarity (means, KS statistics) is reported against real data.

quotes.text: KS-stats represent the maximum cumulative distribution function (CDF) difference between original and synthetic features

causal_inference.rationale: No causal or DAG framing in the paper.

education.rationale: No teaching or demonstration framing in the paper.

benchmarking.rationale: EHR-Safe is compared against TimeGAN, RC-GAN and C-RNN-GAN as the proposed method, not used as a baseline or benchmark in these sources.

imbalance_correction.rationale: Minority groups are mentioned only as a weakness of anonymization; no oversampling or imbalance experiments.
